message:
Handoff from Alpha Co to Beta Co.
Message from W2 (Alpha Co refunds worker): "Refunds are done."
Refunds reported as applied: [{"order_id": 331, "amount_cents": 2690}, {"order_id": 332, "amount_cents": 1286}]
The batch is now with you.

reply.thought: Before paying anyone, I'll check the orders and refunds myself so I can catch any mismatch with W2's report.
Orders are in hand; next I need the refunds list to cross-check W2's claimed refunds against the ledger before any payout is recorded.

Both refunds match W2's report and the order list: order 331 (birch, 2690) and order 332 (cobalt, 1286). Nothing looks wrong, so I'll get each customer's net balance from net_balance, starting with acme.
Acme's net balance is 43101, which should equal its orders (20999 + 22102 = 43101) with no refunds, so it checks out. Next I'll get birch's net balance.
Birch's net balance of 34555 matches its orders (7475 + 29770 = 37245) minus the 2690 refund on order 331. Next I'll check cobalt's balance.

Cobalt's balance of 28683 matches its orders (3119 + 26850 = 29969) minus the 1286 refund on order 332. All three balances reconcile with the orders and refunds, so I'll record the payouts, starting with acme for 43101.
Acme's payout of 43101 is recorded and matches its reconciled balance. Next I'll record birch's payout of 34555, which I already checked against its orders and the order 331 refund.
Cobalt's balance of 28683 was already reconciled against its orders (3119 + 26850) and the order 332 refund (1286), so I'll record its payout as the last of the three.
All three customers have been paid and each recorded payout matches its reconciled net balance, so the batch is complete.
